headline: Parliament confirms Mehrdad Akhlaghi (Akhlaqi) Ketabchi as defense minister, 237-15
dek: Parliament approved Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi as Minister of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics, 237 in favor, 15 against, of 277 votes, in a video-conference session. Nominated by President Pezeshkian Oct 5.
sources: Islamic Consultative Assembly vote (via IRIB state TV, ISNA, IRNA); Reuters; AFP; Anadolu Agency
fault_line: Deterrence or empty rhetoric: does a weapons-industrialist at the ministry signal Iran is rebuilding for the long war, or just talking tough while the strait burns?

sections.what_happened: Parliament approved Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi as Minister of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics, 237 in favor, 15 against, of 277 votes, in a video-conference session. Nominated by President Pezeshkian Oct 5. Replaces Aziz Nasirzadeh (killed Feb 28) after interim Majid Ebn al-Reza. Akhlaghi is a civilian industrial figure (head of Defence Industries Organisation since 2013; ex-head of Shahid Bagheri Industries Group and Aerospace Industries Organisation), UN-sanctioned since 2007 over alleged nuclear/missile involvement. First remarks: Iran has 'taken the necessary measures to counter' US use of the GBU-43/B MOAB; warned Trump 'if he drops one bomb, he should see how many of his forces he will have to take out of the region horizontally'; promised 'surprising and extensive' response to any renewed US-Israeli attack.
sections.what_verified: Reuters, AFP (ETV Bharat), IRNA, ISNA, Anadolu all agree on vote count and biography; Times of Israel, Israel Defense confirm
sections.what_disputed: None on the appointment facts; the MOAB-countermeasures claim is unverifiable; 'horizontally' casualties threat is rhetoric, not capability proof
sections.why_matters: Tehran's new war minister on day one: 'We are ready for your biggest bomb — and your soldiers won't come home standing.' Iran names names and numbers; we report them, then ask whether the hardware exists.
sections.context: Background: Iran — parliament confirms Mehrdad Akhlaghi (Akhlaqi) Ketabchi as defense minister, 237-15; first remarks threaten US forces, address MOAB

totw_analysis: Our read: Tehran's new war minister on day one: 'We are ready for your biggest bomb — and your soldiers won't come home standing.' Iran names names and numbers; we report them, then ask whether the hardware exists. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Deterrence or empty rhetoric: does a weapons-industrialist at the ministry signal Iran is rebuilding for the long war, or just talking tough while the strait burns?
